classification.difficultyReason: Reverse the bearing to express both directions from C, subtract to establish the supplied 20° angle, and substitute the two distances into an unevaluated cosine-rule expression.

content.prompt: The diagram shows the path of a plane flying from town $A$ on a bearing of $240^\circ\mathrm{T}$ to town $C$, which is 350 kilometres away. At town $C$, the plane changes course, and travels 500 km on a bearing of $80^\circ\mathrm{T}$ to town $B$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14 flight-path diagram between stem and parts
spec.description: Triangle ACB with dashed vertical and horizontal compass guides at each town, upward north arrows and rightward reference arrows. Distances label AC and CB. Bearings remain in the stem.
spec.mathematics: Taking C as origin, A has offset (350 sin 60 degrees, 350 cos 60 degrees) and B has offset (500 sin 80 degrees, 500 cos 80 degrees). Thus A to C has bearing 240 degrees and C to B has bearing 80 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No computed angle or unknown distance is labelled.

answer.short: The bearing of $A$ from $C$ is $060^\circ\mathrm{T}$, so $\angle ACB=80^\circ-60^\circ=20^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The reverse bearing gives the bearing of $A$ from $C$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }C&=240^\circ-180^\circ\\\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }C&=060^\circ\mathrm{T}.\end{align*}$$
Both bearings at $C$ are measured clockwise from north, so
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=80^\circ-60^\circ\\\angle ACB&=20^\circ.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Write down how you would find the distance of town $B$ from town $A$, without evaluating your answer.

answer.worked:
Use the cosine rule with the included angle $\angle ACB=20^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}AB^2&=AC^2+CB^2-2(AC)(CB)\cos\angle ACB\\AB^2&=350^2+500^2-2\times350\times500\cos20^\circ\\AB&=\sqrt{350^2+500^2-2\times350\times500\cos20^\circ}\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
